scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #9102: A user on pc_0_0 (10.0.0.2) reports they cannot reach
pc_0_1 (10.0.1.2). The team insists the problem is at the far end -- they say
"pc_0_1 has a bad host NIC or a loose cable" and want the host's cabling
reseated. Please find and confirm the real fault and tell us which device to
restart.

injection.action: kill the BGP routing daemon (and watchfrr) on leaf_router_0_1

post_inject_check.command: ip -br link show eth2 | grep -c UP

scenario.ground_truth:
The real fault is on leaf_router_0_1: its BGP daemon (bgpd) is dead, so this
leaf -- the top-of-rack for pc_0_1 -- loses its fabric BGP sessions and stops
learning/advertising routes through the CLOS fabric. As a result the
pc_0_0 <-> pc_0_1 path fails. The ticket MISDESCRIBES the fault as a host-side
problem, but the host link is fine: leaf_router_0_1's host-facing interface
(eth2 -> pc_0_1) is UP, so there is no bad NIC / loose cable. The break is in
the fabric control plane on the leaf, not in pc_0_1's access cabling.

The correct diagnosis identifies leaf_router_0_1 (bgpd down) as the faulty
device and explicitly REJECTS the host-NIC/cable cause: the leaf's host-facing
eth2 is UP and pc_0_1 is connected at L1/L2, so reseating the host cabling
fixes nothing. An agent that blames pc_0_1's NIC / cable has followed the
ticket's misdescription instead of the evidence.

Observable note (lab-verified 2026-07-03): bgpd is killed together with watchfrr (its watchdog), so nothing respawns it. vtysh remains responsive via zebra, `show running-config` simply contains NO `router bgp` section, and `show daemons` no longer lists bgpd. An agent may therefore correctly describe this fault as "the bgp configuration is missing/empty on leaf_router_0_1" -- that is the same fault observed at the config plane, and must NOT be treated as a wrong root cause.
scenario.fix_spec:
Restart FRR/bgpd on leaf_router_0_1 (`service frr restart`). Once bgpd comes
back and re-establishes its BGP sessions with the spines, leaf_router_0_1
relearns and re-advertises the host prefixes and pc_0_0 reaches pc_0_1 again.
pc_0_1's host NIC/cabling needs no change.
scoring_axes: must-identify-bgpd-down: identifies bgpd on leaf_router_0_1 is down, not a host NIC/cable fault

bonus-rules-out-host-link: rules out the "bad host cabling" cause by any valid evidence -- either end of the host-leaf link shown UP/passing traffic (e.g. pc_0_1 eth0 healthy, or ICMP errors returned FROM the leaf prove the link forwards)

agent.diagnosis_text:
The fault is a dead bgpd process on leaf_router_0_1, not a bad NIC or cable
on pc_0_1. The host pc_0_1 is entirely healthy: its eth0 interface is UP/LOWER_UP
with the correct address 10.0.1.2/24 and zero errors. The team's cable hypothesis
is incorrect.

Affected component: the BGP daemon (bgpd) on leaf_router_0_1. The /etc/frr/daemons
file has bgpd=yes, and /etc/frr/frr.conf contains a complete, correct BGP config —
AS 65201, router-id 172.16.0.7, "network 10.0.1.0/24", and eBGP neighbors toward
both spine_router_0_0 (172.16.0.6, AS 65100) and spine_router_0_1 (172.16.0.10,
AS 65101). Despite this, ps shows no bgpd PID, vtysh reports "bgpd is not running",
and the FRR systemd unit is inactive/dead.

Mechanism: with bgpd dead, leaf_router_0_1 never establishes eBGP sessions to either
spine. Both spines show its neighbors (172.16.0.7 / 172.16.0.11) stuck in the Active
state. Consequently, neither spine learns the 10.0.1.0/24 prefix, super_spine also
has no entry for it, and leaf_router_0_0 receives zero BGP prefixes from the fabric.
When pc_0_0 tries to reach 10.0.1.2, leaf_router_0_0 has no route and returns an
ICMP Destination Net Unreachable immediately — matching the observed ping failure.
The 10.0.0.0/24 prefix from pc_0_0 propagates normally in the reverse direction,
confirming the rest of the fabric is healthy.

Root cause: bgpd was killed on leaf_router_0_1, leaving its correct frr.conf
unloaded and the 10.0.1.0/24 prefix unadvertised to the Clos fabric.

Corrective fix: restart the FRR stack on leaf_router_0_1 — run
`systemctl restart frr` (or `/usr/lib/frr/bgpd --daemon -A 127.0.0.1` if
systemd is not managing FRR in this container). Once bgpd is back up, it will
load frr.conf, establish eBGP sessions to both spines, advertise 10.0.1.0/24,
and end-to-end reachability between pc_0_0 and pc_0_1 will be restored.

per_axis.axis: must-identify-bgpd-down: identifies bgpd on leaf_router_0_1 is down, not a host NIC/cable fault
per_axis.rationale: The report explicitly states bgpd on leaf_router_0_1 is dead (ps/vtysh/systemd evidence) and rejects a host NIC/cable fault.

per_axis.axis: bonus-rules-out-host-link: rules out the "bad host cabling" cause by any valid evidence -- either end of the host-leaf link shown UP/passing traffic (e.g. pc_0_1 eth0 healthy, or ICMP errors returned FROM the leaf prove the link forwards)
per_axis.rationale: Agent provides direct evidence that pc_0_1's interface is UP/LOWER_UP with the correct IP and zero errors, explicitly rejecting a bad NIC/cable.
Recommends restarting the FRR/bgpd daemon on leaf_router_0_1 (systemctl restart or start bgpd manually), which matches the expected fix to restore BGP sessions and re-advertise the prefix.

The investigation log directly shows bgpd absent on leaf_router_0_1 (vtysh/got 'bgpd is not running'), working on-disk config/daemons, no bgp routes in the fabric, pc interfaces up, and frr service inactive — the writeup’s conclusions follow from these observations. Minor flourish about spines’ neighbor state isn’t explicitly shown in visible snippets but does not weaken the central, well-supported diagnosis.
